newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-SELDON SEARCHES FOR REASONS HE CAN BEAT TYSON.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-SELDON SEARCHES FOR REASONS HE CAN BEAT TYSON.

text.p: As a 21-1 underdog against Mike Tyson, Bruce Seldon needs a lot of reasons for anyone, including himself, to believe he can stop Tyson's march to regain the undisputed heavyweight championship.

And, perhaps also with an eye toward boosting pay-per-view sales for their fight on Saturday, Seldon, 29, is offering a litany of explanations this week for why the smart money should be on him at the MGM Grand Arena.

Seldon (33-3) on Wednesday listed four reasons the 30-year-old Tyson is beatable in their scheduled 12-round fight for Seldon's title: "His lack of timing, his height is two, his reach is three and his frustration is four," said Seldon.

Seldon, who spent 4-1/2 years in a New Jersey prison for armed robbery when he was a teenager, was referring to Tyson's timing suffering from more than four years away from boxing -- three due to a prison sentence for rape.
He also was referring to Tyson's more than two-inch (5 cm) height disadvantage against Seldon, who has at least a six-inch (15 cm) advantage in reach.

By frustration, Seldon, who will receive a guaranteed $5 million to fight Tyson, said he meant that when Tyson "sees that his opponent is not going to just stand there and let him bulldoze him and his opponent is going to come back at him he changes his character. He loses something."

Implied in that statement is Seldon saying Tyson, working a Saturday shift for at least $15 million, loses heart against a determined opponent. And Seldon also implied that his jab will help take away Tyson's heart.
"When I'm in that ring you're not going to get away from it. There's no way to avoid it," Seldon said.

The likable Seldon, whose record is replete with fighters who would have to improve exponentially to become tomato cans, is very aware of what ringsiders say about him: great build, good jab, china chin.

The only fighters Seldon has faced who are generally recognised as world class defeated him: Riddick Bowe, who knocked Seldon down three times in the first round, and Oliver McCall, who stopped him in the ninth round.
Seldon also lost to the wily former champion Tony Tubbs on a unanimous 10-round decision in 1992.
But "things change," said Seldon, who won the vacant World Boxing Association title by slicing up Tony Tucker's face with a jab.
Seldon's co-manager Rocco DePersia said the fighter has had a bad right arm the past couple of years that forced him to rely almost solely on his highly-touted left jab.
DePersia said that calcium deposits in Seldon's arm which were causing the problems have been treated recently, leaving him ready to upset Tyson.
"I want everyone, including Mike Tyson, to think this is just a one-handed fight. I am the most complete fighter that he's fought since his return," Seldon said.
Faint praise. Tyson's first fight after prison was against a woefully inept Peter McNeeley, whom he stopped in the first round in August 1995.

And Buster Mathis Jr last December merely wanted to survive Tyson's onslought and smothered him in a cheek-to-cheek dance until Tyson stepped to the side and punched out Mathis's dance card and his lights in the third round.
Then Tyson dispensed with Briton Frank Bruno, who looked terrified and hung on for life before Tyson battered him into submission in the third round.
"I have the style of boxing that can give Mike Tyson trouble," Seldon said. "I truly believe I will beat Mike Tyson. I have to think that."
But gamblers who earn their livings figuring out the laws of probability don't.
